target: Living Notch and embedded command tray usability

contract.purpose: Make the Living Notch a fast, calm command surface for everyday Pace use.
contract.canonicalPurpose: Pace helps a Mac user ask, understand, and act through a private on-device voice agent.
contract.audience: A Mac user using voice or text while staying focused on their current work.
contract.job: Show Pace's state, then let the user issue and follow one request without layout friction or dead air.
contract.thesis: Preserve the measured hardware notch and let the same black surface expand edge-to-edge into the command tray.
contract.system: Local Signal Desk: graphite and black surfaces, system typography, electric blue for local activity, semantic state colors, and a 4-point spacing rhythm.
contract.signature: The exact physical camera housing remains centered while the same clipped surface grows into the tray.
contract.risk: Removing the nested gutter could make the tray feel dense, so content keeps 12 to 14 point internal padding while the outer notch owns the silhouette.

projectCheck.command: bash scripts/test-pace.sh PaceChatSessionTests PaceNativeInterfaceModelTests PaceIntentClassifierTests LocalPlannerClientThinkingStripperTests

findings: The SwiftUI detector returned no findings, but the generic fallback is advisory-only for native Swift surfaces.
Browser overlay inspection is not applicable to the native AppKit panel.

ownerFeedback.note: The existing Pace design system was preserved while the user-requested notch usability defects were corrected.
